ai.title: Add checkpointing to fine-tuning dataset generation script
ai.summary: scripts/generate-fine-tuning-dataset.ts now saves intermediate progress to dataset_progress.json and resumes from existing entries. Switched from manual batching to mapAsync for concurrency. Added pytorch, linux, nushell, and vscode to PROJECTS_LIST. Increased NUMBER_OF_COMMITS to 3000 and FILES_TO_PROCESS to 1000. Removed ANTHROPIC_API_KEY check from createDataset.

eli5.text: The script that builds example conversations for training the coding assistant now saves its work as it goes, so if it stops partway through, it can pick up where it left off instead of starting over from scratch. It also checks more software projects for code changes to learn from, and it processes files in a more organized way that's quicker. The assistant itself already has this smarter behavior built in starting today.

ai.title: Tweak fine-tuning script params
ai.summary: Adjusts `scripts/generate-fine-tuning-dataset.ts` to optimize dataset generation. Increases `NUMBER_OF_COMMITS` to 5000, decreases `PARALLEL_PROCESSES` to 5, and adds a 50k token limit per file using `countTokens`. Updates `BLACK_LIST_STRINGS` to exclude more autogenerated files and shifts train/validation split to 90/10.

eli5.text: The tool that builds the AI's training data now looks at more real-world code (5,000 examples instead of 3,000) but processes it more carefully, using fewer workers and skipping huge files to avoid slowdowns. The final lessons are split differently - more for practice, less for testing - and the system ignores a couple more types of auto-written files. If you were training an assistant, your dataset would be larger, cleaner, and organized with a tighter test set, but you wouldn't notice anything different in the finished assistant.
